I think overall it is fun, it is addictive at least. I sometimes get losing streaks but I still find it enjoyable, most of the time even if I lose I still make positive income with the in gam currency so it's not that big of a deal unless I am trying to grind for something to buy or research. But I think the game is pretty cool, they have a program for veterans so you can get some perks and a neat badge next to your name. I haven't spent a lot of money maybe only around ~$20 in the time I have played and that's just because I like having female commanders so I pick them up sometimes if there's an event going on with them available. Sometimes the matchmaking can take a while though it kinda just depends, sometimes I can get in within seconds and other times it can take up to 10-15 minutes for some reason.

Played this game since 2013 on xbox, switched to PC 2 years ago and decided to download it on steam. Big mistake.

We'll start with no account migration. You should be able to choose to migrate your account to a different platform 1 time. Especially considering how much money you have to blow on this game to get anywhere meaningful without spending inordinate amounts of time playing. I guess that would kill wargamings chance to get me to spend hundreds of dollars again.

WG had the brilliant idea to increase the HP pool for lower tier tanks, all that means is that tank destroyers (which have almost no armor at lower tiers) are completely fucked. Sure you got some more HP but so does your more heavily armored opponent. Chances of getting screwed? 100%.

WG's ranked and new battlemode "art of war" are restricted to tier 10. Just another way to force new players to really open their wallets if the want to participate in anything other than random battles.
You cant log in with your wargaming account. You cant recover your email address. Just very poor infrastructure.

This game i have played for over 20000 battles at 6 minutes average length and i can tell you this:
- The game is itself is good on average
- the worst aspect of the game is the skillgap. If youre a new player, prepare Uranus (the planet).
- If you want to commit yourself to the game expect the following : Need to research what is good, what is bad and how to play each tank properly depending on its strengths. At least 3 tier 8 premium tanks are required after you go further than tier 8, due to the economy of the game tanking your income in to negatives if you play higher tiers or use expensive ammo.
Then and ONLY then is when i recommend this game, if you truly like the experience and want to play daily for at least half an hour. Doing so will speed up your progress significantly, especially if you use premium account.

The game has its flaws, but overall provides great fun, especially when playing with other people in a platoon.

It has many flaws, but it's still a game one can relax with (if you can ignore the tryhards and the mentally unstable individuals)
The main problem is developers ignoring the community.

Despite all the complaints from the WoT community about WG, this game still satisfies arcade tank-on-tank competitive gaming. Not comparable to WT (apples and oranges and whatnot), but better than Blitz, and although I prefer the WoT Console version more for balance, I enjoy the original PC version.

7/10 Graphics
6/10 Sound Effects
6/10 Matchmaking
7/10 Online Player Base

This is a unique wildlife reserve where grown men pay real money to sit in a bush and listen to artillery turn them into scrap metal in one shot. Your only goal is to tolerate the 14 idiots on your team who throw the match in two minutes while you’re trying to hit a single pixel on the turret of some other miserable nerd. It’s the only game where the phrase "we didn't even scratch them" triggers more PTSD than an actual midlife crisis.

While 'team diff' is inevitable in every online game, WoT's vast battlefields, extremely long TTK, large player counts, and distinct role divisions all act as pressures that raise team dependency to unprecedented levels.

Teamwork is lacking even in games with 4 or 5 players. You and your team of 14 chimpanzees will not be able to perform any strategic actions against people who don't touch grass and only eat, poop, and play WoT.

Indeed there are still ways to resolve this, such as by running event battles even more than now, but if you want a healthy hobby, WoT is not for you. I can't play this game anymore because of hypertension.
good game if your into a arcade type game but if you want a realistic game, play Warthunder.

Gameplay is fun and you can easily spend hours going through match after match. If you're not interested in spending money on this game, you do have to be careful not to get sucked into the P2W schemes because it can be really tempting. It's hard to keep up with the P2W players sometimes, although you can be plenty competitive through F2P or with a few dollars here and there. But it does take time and dedication. Overall, I do recommend for fans of tank warfare due to its sheer fun.

Tanks are cool and this game is beautiful but the gameplay is garbage. The game mostly decides the winners and losers because your aim, damage, module damage, and armor penetration are all decided by RNG. There are also unbalanced maps, artillery, and a few overpowered tanks. I immediately downloaded this on Steam because it sorta' felt new again by coming here but I was quickly reminded of how bad it is. Also bad ping for most of us in the USA because the playerbase is barely big enough for ONE server in all of North America. I want to love this game but it disappoints me every time.

First of all, I love this game.

However, Wargaming has just put a nail in World of Tanks' coffin. They have made it 100% pay-to-win by releasing overpowered Tier X tanks and putting them behind three tiers of loot boxes. These tanks are, in almost every way, better than their free-to-play counterparts, and you would have to spend hundreds of dollars to acquire them.

With this move, they will destroy the game's balance and will be unable to restore it because they refuse to nerf tanks that were sold for real money.

Usually, if you were considering starting the game, I would gladly tell you to give it a try and see if it clicks with you. But given this dire prospect, I would have to say: don't start.

Pay to win. Massive disadvantage unless you fork out the money. Great during promotion times, or eg at christmas, but otherwise you are always running out of cash in game and at a disadvantage in matchmaking. Pity really because its a nice game in theory.

The pay to win aspect is a big problem. The most expensive rounds are roughly 2000 of the basic currency while the others barely break 100. It wouldn't be as much as an issue if 5 or so of those rounds cost more than you would get after a match. (regardless of if you win or lose.) This gives player that pay money for easy access to these rounds have a massive advantage over free to play players. Another issue is that long time or high tier player will usually have a stock pile of credits, and will often go to lower tiers to pub stomp newer players. It really makes the early game grind miserable.
Its fun, can be frustrating and very grindy xD but its a game you can chill with :)

World of Tanks is a captivating multiplayer online game that puts you in command of powerful tanks, engaging you in intense battles against players from around the world. As an avid gamer and a fan of strategic warfare, I've found World of Tanks to be a compelling experience overall.

Version 2.0 is WORSE than the old version. Matchmaking is a joke in 90% of the games. BOTs are just out of control and WoT does nothing to control them, in fact they encourage them to boost up their numbers that is why you see so many. Usually 4 or 5 min BOTs per game T8 and above. In at least 30% of matchmaking games you are fighting in are tanks 2 tiers above your level which makes it no fun trying to pen their armor.

what a complete waste of time! if you enjoy only controlling 1 aspect (positioning) of a game, all the while, your hit rate, penetration rate, and damage will be determined by a broken 'RNG' system, then this is the hot mess you're looking for! There is nothing 'Random' about hitting and penning 30% of the time, but getting penned 80% of the time.... consistently. I have wasted over 1200 hours thinking something will change. Been gaming for many many years, i know my abilities, they are slightly above average, but this trash is beyond bad!! Not hard to see why WG.net is a 1 hit wonder game developer. On the other hand, the graphics are great and the control is smooth. A perfect way to distract from the complete incompetence with respect to balance.

Veteran since 2015, took a break and came back 3yrs later. Some people say its P2W but I don't see it. It's more like gambling. A lot of times it will feel rigged as many have pointed out. Matches often times end in the first 3 minutes, giving you no chance other than being a punching xp bag. To keep it short here is my list of issues with the game.

1. Spot mechanics
2. RNG
3. MM
4. tank balance
5. Gold spammers
6. Map layout
7. Arty

Those will be your biggest enemies. I could go into detail on each one but that will some time, plus there are other reviews pointing out at those issues. So, no I don't recommend this game. If you are new you will have to grind a lot, learn the tanks roles which often times it won't really matter and be in a world of pain. Just recently WG is giving a free tier X line as a tease. If you are a veteran coming back after a long absent you know what to expect because nothing has change really.

A mess of stuff just piled on top of eachother.

Want to look at challenges? Oh, wait 6-8 seconds for the game to load them.

I'm not sure if i will continue playing once my premium account days run out though. BTW 360 premium account days cost almost $100. Might as well play the new COD every year instead.

Fun tank game. Steep learning curve when getting into real battles with other players. Does seem fairly monetized, but so far at the low tier of vehicle I'm in, it doesn't seem to affect gameplay much, yet.

Also, I am noting that I am only reviewing this for the free stuff you get for the review. Even so, it's still a decent and fun game. Looks beautiful.

reason.text: Negative reviews from this period focus on loot boxes, with reviewers calling them gambling and describing a new tiered system.
Reviews describe the loot boxes as "predatory" and add that the game feels pay to win.

lines.F1: World of Tanks had a negative surge (far more negative reviews than usual, often called a review bomb), May 2025
lines.F2: May 2025: 18% positive across 955 reviews (786 negative), against a usual 71% positive and 82 negative a month
lines.R3: (negative review, 1h played) "New low for lootboxes, avoid this game. WG, look at Chems WoT reform youtube video on how to fix your dying game"
lines.R8: (negative review, 243h played) "The new tiered loot boxes are merely a scam. I can't recommend a game that is trying to scam its players."
lines.R10: (negative review, 20h played) "Absolutely disgusting and predatory Gambling Crates within Gambling Crates withing Gambling Crates, ultra late pity system and full on Pay 2 Win rewards that are atrociously overpowered and thus highly desirable."
lines.R13: (negative review, 58h played) "One of the worst games on steam... its pay to win and random battles are full of bots with rigged rng Go to hell Wargambling... btw there is no such thing as skill, just RNG and your wallet"
lines.R14: (negative review, 734h played) "Lootboxes were bad enough, now theres a 3 tiered lootbox system? Greedy ass wargaming. Instead of fixing your game, you milk it Nobody should play world of tanks. Do not play this game. Wargaming does not respect you"
lines.R15: (negative review, 10h played) "Latest lootbox event crossed the line, revert the changes please."

tldr.text: Mostly Positive (73%): players praise the gameplay and combat.
The biggest complaint is the price and monetization, which 21% of reviews criticize.

details.text: Players who review early are far less positive than those who stay longer, with 28% positive against 81%.
Recent reviews complain less about the price and monetization than before, while complaints about the community have grown.
